rows.02:6fb8:
"Is that so?
That's just the kind of child I'm fond of.
So pretty, and yet your nature is the very opposite, eh?
Those looks are the only thing you've got going for you."
rows.02:7040:
Hara couldn't help bristling at that.
"Who's the one who isn't cute here?
Whatever, just hurry up and hand over the candy already☆"
Hara practically tore a candy out of the old lady's basket and ran off.{p}
rows.02:70fc:
"My, my, what an impatient child.
Well, I suppose that's that child's fate as well..."{p}
rows.02:7158:
When Hara got home, she hurried to her room and locked the door.
"I can't wait to see the looks on everyone's faces. Hee hee."
Then she slowly sucked on the candy.
A few days later...{p}
rows.02:7288:
They say her eyes slanted up, her mouth bent down into a scowl, deep creases dug in between her brows, and her face warped into a mean-looking one.
Just like Hara's heart, see.
Apparently the candies the old lady hands out come in different kinds.
They say she picks out the candy that suits each person.
That's why things work out pretty well for everyone, I guess.
The candy Hara tore out of the old lady's basket was apparently one that makes your heart show up in your looks, just as it is.{p}
rows.02:74a4:
What happened to Hara after that, you ask?
She got plastic surgery and finally got her own face back, they say, and she was so moved by it, y'know.
She turned over a new leaf, studied her butt off, and got into medical school.
Apparently she wanted to become a plastic surgeon herself.
These days, they say Dr. Hara's gotten so famous she's one of the top five in all of Japan.
I guess you could say that's thanks to the old lady, in a way.{p}
rows.02:7624:
But hey, a candy like that would be fun, wouldn't it?
You'd want to make your teachers, your friends, your sweetheart eat one, right?
You'd wanna know what they're really like...
...That's the end of my story.
Let's have the next one tell theirs.{p}
rows.02:76e4:
"I didn't really do anything in particular.
Before I knew it, I'd just ended up like this."
"Oh, really...?"
Partly because Hara had been making fun of her all this time, if never to her face, Katagiri had decided she'd never tell Hara the truth.
Then one day,{p}
rows.02:77cc:
"My skin's lost its firmness somehow..."
Katagiri noticed something was wrong with her.
No matter how much she ate, she didn't put on weight.
That much was fine, but no matter how much she ate, she just kept getting thinner and thinner.{p}
rows.02:7894:
Her cheeks went gaunt and hollow, her eyes sank into her head, and in the end she was bedridden.
Her family urged her to go to the hospital, but she flat out refused.
I think she was scared that if this condition got cured, she'd go right back to being fat like before.
Meanwhile, one night, she felt the skin all over her body start to itch and crawl.{p}
rows.02:79f8:
When she looked closely, she could clearly see something moving under the thin layer of her skin.
In a frenzy, she pulled something out of the closet.
"Take that☆"
In a frenzy, she stabbed the squirming thing with a needle.
Right through her own skin.
"It's still squirming.
Here too...
And there, and even way over here...
Take that, take that, take thaaat☆"{p}
rows.02:7b70:
She died the next morning.
With needles stuck all over her body...
It had been only a week since she took to her bed.
When they did the autopsy at the hospital, they found parasites crawling around inside her, and their eggs laid thick all through her body.
Just picturing them squirming everywhere, in her organs, in her blood vessels, in every last part of her, sends a chill down your spine, huh?
The reason she'd been getting thin was that the parasites were sucking up all her nutrients.
Seems it's not like every single person who sucked on the Candy Granny's candy got to be happy.
Every now and then you draw a dud like this one.
Well, I guess you could say your choice was the right one too, in a way...
...That's the end of my story.
Let's have the next one tell theirs.{p}
rows.02:7de0:
"I've been waiting for you!
Granny!
C'mon, hurry up and gimme some candy.
That's why you showed up in front of me, right?"
I guess even a contrarian like Sakuma couldn't help letting his true feelings slip.
"Ho ho, aren't you an impatient one.
No need to rush so, the candy won't run away.
Hmm, from one look at you, dearie, I'd say you're quite the twisted one.
Poor thing, you must have led a truly miserable life."
With somebody saying that to him, there was no way Sakuma wasn't gonna get ticked off.{p}
rows.02:7f90:
"Shut up already.
I take it back☆
Why the hell do I have to hear that from some stranger like you☆
Just get lost☆"
He blurted it out before he could stop himself.
Every time, right after he says something like that, he thinks, Oh crap☆
but by then it's too late.
That's how he keeps screwing everything up.{p}
rows.02:8098:
"Don't be so cold to me, now.
You see, I only ever appear before you once.
Just once, in your whole long life.
Don't you think it's a waste to throw that away yourself?
So please don't talk to me like that."
The old lady peered up at Sakuma with upturned eyes.{p}So, what do you think Sakuma did?
rows.02:81c8: Says he wanted to meet her
rows.02:81fc:
"Fo fo fo, honest, that's a good child.
I'm fond of children who say what they mean."
That's what she said, grinning at him.
When you got a good look at her, the old lady was way filthier than the rumors said.
Her eyes were caked with gunk, her teeth were crusted thick with plaque, and when she looked at you with those unfocused eyes, it sent a chill right through you.
Little by little, he couldn't stand it anymore, and before he knew it,{p}
rows.02:8428: Before she could even finish, Sakuma all but snatched the candy from her and ran off.{p}
rows.02:84f0:
Sakuma flew home and locked himself in his room.
He took deep breaths to calm his pounding heart, unwrapped the candy, and popped it into his mouth in one go.{p}
rows.02:859c:
"...S-so good☆
This is incredible☆
Th-this taste☆"
He sucked on it for a while, then, out of habit, crunched it up with a crack and ate the whole thing.{p}
rows.02:8638:
See, what the old lady had been trying to tell him back then was that you have to suck this candy all the way down without biting into it...
If you ever bit into it, your sense of taste would go haywire, and for the rest of your life, whatever you ate, it would taste like nothing but that candy.
For Sakuma, who never learned the meaning of patience, I think that would've been a bit much.
Even if the old lady had told him about it.
If he'd just held out a little, he might've lived happily for the rest of his life.
After that, nobody saw the Candy Granny again.
Maybe she'd moved on to the next school.
As for Sakuma, whatever he ate, good food, fresh food, nasty food, rotten food, it all tasted like that candy, and finally he went out of his mind.
I mean, no matter how good the candy is, if everything tastes like that, come on...{p}
rows.02:8918: In the end, they say, he cut off his own tongue with a box cutter.{p}
rows.02:89f4:
The second he said that, he yanked the guy's tongue out and sliced it clean off with the box cutter!
Sakuma pulled his own rotting, maggot-infested tongue out of his pocket and sewed it onto the stump of the guy's tongue.
With red cotton thread...
And of course, he sewed the tongue he'd cut off onto the stump of his own rotting tongue, too.
Then he stuck his tongue out at the mirror and said,{p}
rows.02:8d10:
"Something feels off."
The student slowly sat up in bed and got up to get a drink of water.
They turned on the faucet, and the instant they went to drink from the cup...
rows.02:8db4: They dropped the cup before they knew it.{p}
rows.02:8df4:
In the mirror in front of them, inside their mouth, was a tongue that wasn't their own, sewn on with red thread.
And behind them stood Sakuma, laughing and flicking his red tongue in and out, they say.{p}
rows.02:8eac:
Oh yeah, they say if you suck on candy at school, Sakuma will swap out your tongue.
"You wanna suck on candy that bad?"
That's what he says while he does it...
So, if Sakuma ever says that to you, what do you do...{p}
rows.02:8f7c:
You bite down on the candy you're sucking, as hard as you can☆
If you don't, you'll get your tongue cut off too.
...That's the end of my story.
Let's have the next one tell theirs.{p}
rows.02:9018:
He's a total idiot, seriously.
That Sakuma, I mean.
rows.02:9054:
He should've left it alone, but he just couldn't help opening it.
The urge to look at something scary, I guess.{p}
rows.02:90c0:
And sure enough, there stood the old lady.
"I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I ate all the candy, please forgive me.
I'll do anything☆"
He got down on his hands and knees, head to the floor, and apologized for all he was worth.
"Is that so?
Well, what's been eaten can't be helped.
I'll forgive you, just this once."
Sakuma practically jumped for joy.
"But there's a condition.
I'm getting on in years.
My body won't do as it's told anymore. Won't you help me make my candy?"
If that was all it took to be forgiven, it'd be a piece of cake, he figured, so he agreed to help.
"So, um, what exactly do I have to do?"{p}
rows.02:92d8:
"You found out when you ate them, I expect, dearie. They were very tasty, weren't they?
And no wonder.
The ingredients are different...
You see, I use real eyeballs.
They don't call it eye candy for nothing.
rows.02:93a0:
Hee hee hee..."
"Gah☆
Th-those were human eyeballs★
I ate eyeballs☆"
Sakuma felt like he was about to pass out.
"So you see, I want you to go and fetch the ingredients for me.
From now on, forever and ever."{p}
rows.02:949c:
After that, they say, no one ever saw Sakuma again.
And another thing: you must never think, or say out loud, that you want to suck on the old lady's candy.{p}
rows.02:95dc:
It's enough to drive you crazy, right?
You'll just have to grit your teeth and hold out.
Oh, come to think of it, you said you wanted to eat it a little while ago, didn't you?
But hey, if Sakuma does come, there's just one way to save yourself.
Sakuma will say,
"Give me your eyeballs,"
so shut your eyes and say,
"I took three candies from the old lady too.
So I have no two eyeballs to give you."
That's what you say.
Don't get it wrong...
...That's the end of my story.
Let's have the next one tell theirs.{p}
rows.02:978c:
Oh yeah, you definitely said it, didn't you.
They say anyone who hears this story and says they want to eat the Candy Granny's candy gets to meet her.
Sometime in the next month, somewhere, you'll run into her.
It's too late now.
You already said it.
But there's one way to save yourself.
Within two days of the day you said you wanted to suck on her candy, you have to get ten more people to say, 'I want to suck on candy.'
Do that, and the old lady won't come for you.
Huh? Yeah, same goes for me.
Truth is, you're number ten.
...That's the end of my story.
Let's have the next one tell theirs.{p}
rows.02:997c:
Huh?
You're a lucky one, huh?
Man, I can't believe there's somebody who doesn't know that pain.
There's the pain of the cavity itself, but then the sound of the drill when they fix it puts you in a lousy mood too.
That shrill whiiiiiine.
The faint smell of your teeth getting ground down.
Just thinking about it gives me the shakes.
.........Anyway, I got off track.
Point is, it's rough.
And it was the same for Katagiri.{p}
rows.02:9ac4:
So if you don't hate candy...
you're just being contrary, huh?
...Hey.{p}Deep down, you really want to try it, don't you?
rows.02:9b48: I don't want to eat it
rows.02:9b6c:
You're still saying that★
You're a stubborn one.
I bet deep down you really do want to try it...
Well, enjoy saying that while you still can.{p}
rows.02:9c10:
They say the Candy Granny just loves contrarians like you.
I mean it.
They say she's shown up in front of twisted types like that time and time again.
To give them candy...?
Sorry, wrong answer.
Let's see...
Say, just for the sake of argument, you met the Candy Granny...
"You've been waiting for me, haven't you, dearie?"{p}If she asked you that, what would you say?
rows.02:9d90:
Figured.
That's what you would say.
Even if, deep down, you were dying to meet her.
...'Cause you're a contrarian.{p}
rows.02:9e18:
They say when she shows up in front of a twisted type, the Candy Granny's basket is empty.
Because she has no intention of giving them any candy.
When she meets someone like you, this is what the Candy Granny says:
"Your eyes don't show things as they truly are, dearie.
There's no use in keeping eyeballs like those."
And then the Candy Granny's hands grab your face tight, and...☆{p}
rows.02:9f78:
She takes those eyes of yours away.
...Ha ha ha.
Don't sulk like that.
It's just a 'what if,' right?{p}
rows.02:9ffc:
But y'know.
This story isn't made up.
The senior who told me this story was famous for being a real twisted type, but...
These days, that senior always wears sunglasses.{p}
rows.02:a0a4:
Why, you ask?
One look at the face under those sunglasses and you'd know right away.
The gaping black holes where the eyes should be.
It's no big deal for a guy like me, but you'd better watch out.
For the Candy Granny, I mean.
I told you she was really around until five or six years ago, right?
Just because there aren't rumors about her doesn't mean she isn't still out there.
Today, maybe...
Looks like it's gonna be pretty late by the time we head home.
You going home alone?
Then you'd better be real careful.
...Right, that's the end of my story.
Go on to the next one.{p}
rows.02:a264:
Huh, now that's a surprise.
I wouldn't have thought a contrarian like you would answer that honestly.
But y'know, it's no good just covering it up with the right answer for the moment.
The Candy Granny sees right through a person's true nature at a glance.
No matter how hard you try to hide it, it's no use.{p}
